newsitem.title: USA: Pfizer sees possible 98 launch for Viagra.
newsitem.headline: Pfizer sees possible 98 launch for Viagra.

text.p: Pfizer Inc said on Thursday it had completed clinical trials for its drug Viagra for treating male impotence and expected to file for its approval with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration later this year.
The filing will make "a 1998 U.S. launch of Viagra a real possibility," John Niblack, Pfizer research and development executive vice president, told the company's annual shareholder meeting.

Viagra is an oral drug and would compete against Pharmacia & Upjohn's Caverject, which involves an injection into the penis, and Vivus Inc's MUSE system, which uses a single-dose applicator of a drug that increases blood flow.
The company said it anticipates its broad-spectrum antibiotic Trovan gaining FDA approval by late 1997 or early 1998.

Last month Pfizer filed its drug Zeldox, for treating psychotic symptoms including schizophrenia, Niblack said. The company expects to file its dofetilide drug for treating abnormal heart rhythms by the end of this year.

Niblack said the company was launching a worldwide construction program that will add one million square feet of laboratory space to the company's facilities. Pfizer expects to spend $2.0 billion in research and development this year.
